s: Under the Palas, which centre became associated with translating books into Tibetan?
x: Jagaddala was associated with translations into Tibetan, while Buddhist texts were compiled at Nalanda under Dharmapala.

s: Where is the Somapura Mahavihara located at present?
x: Somapura Mahavihara is at Paharpur in Naogaon district, Bangladesh. Antichak is Vikramashila, Varendra is Jagaddala and Bihar Sharif is Odantapuri.

s: Nalanda University in Bihar was founded in which century AD?
x: Nalanda was founded in the 5th century AD by the Gupta ruler Kumaragupta I.

s: Vikramashila Mahavihara, at Antichak, lies in which district of Bihar?
x: Vikramashila is at Antichak in Bhagalpur district, not Banka (BPSC 2023 trap).

s:
Consider the following statements about the destruction of Pala-period centres of learning:
1. Their destruction by Bakhtiyar Khilji is generally placed around 1193–1200.
2. One tradition gives 1194 for the destruction of Nalanda.
3. Jagaddala was sacked in the early eleventh century.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The destruction is placed around 1193–1200, with 1194 for Nalanda in one tradition. Jagaddala was sacked in the early thirteenth century, not the eleventh.

s: Where is the Odantapuri Mahavihara located at present?
x: Odantapuri, built by Gopala, was at Bihar Sharif in Bihar.

s:
Consider the following statements about Vikramashila Mahavihara:
1. It was founded by Dharmapala.
2. It lies in Banka district of Bihar.
3. It was a centre of Tantric (Vajrayana) Buddhism.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Vikramashila was founded by Dharmapala and was a Vajrayana centre. It lies at Antichak in Bhagalpur district, not Banka.

s: Who founded the Nalanda Mahavihara?
x: Nalanda was founded by the Gupta ruler Kumaragupta I in the 5th century AD; the Palas only patronised it.

s: In which year was the foundation of the Nava Nalanda Mahavihara laid?
x: Bhikshu Jagadish Kashyap laid the foundation of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara on 20 November 1951.

s: Which mahavihara was founded by Gopala, the first Pala king?
x: Gopala built Odantapuri (Bihar Sharif); Vikramashila and Somapura were founded by Dharmapala and Jagaddala by Ramapala.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Mahavihara) - List-II (Founder)
A. Nalanda - 1. Ramapala
B. Odantapuri - 2. Dharmapala
C. Vikramashila - 3. Kumaragupta I
D. Jagaddala - 4. Gopala
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Nalanda was founded by Kumaragupta I, Odantapuri by Gopala, Vikramashila by Dharmapala and Jagaddala by Ramapala.

s: In which region was the Jagaddala Mahavihara, founded by Ramapala, located?
x: Jagaddala, founded by Ramapala, was in Varendra, now in Naogaon, Bangladesh.

s: Who laid the foundation of the Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1951?
x: The Nava Nalanda Mahavihara was founded by Bhikshu Jagadish Kashyap (foundation 20 November 1951).

s: By what name do Tibetan sources call the five great monasteries of the Pala period together?
x: Nalanda, Odantapuri, Vikramashila, Somapura and Jagaddala together are called the Panchamahavihara.

s: Which mahavihara, founded by Gopala, became a model for the monasteries of Tibet?
x: Odantapuri at Bihar Sharif, founded by Gopala, with about 12,000 monks, was a model for Tibetan monasteries.

s: Which of the following acharya – association pairs is correctly matched?
o: Shantarakshita – Founded Samye monastery in Tibet
Sakya Sri Bhadra – Head of Nalanda in Harsha's time
x: Shantarakshita of Nalanda founded Samye monastery in Tibet. Shilabhadra headed Nalanda in Harsha's time, Atisha was linked with Vikramashila and Sakya Sri Bhadra with Jagaddala.

s: Which one of the following was NOT an acharya associated with the Buddhist mahaviharas such as Nalanda and Vikramashila?
x: Kautilya was not a Nalanda acharya (BPSC 2025 trap). Shilabhadra headed Nalanda in Harsha's time, Shantarakshita of Nalanda founded Samye monastery in Tibet, and Atisha of Vikramashila revived Buddhism in Tibet.

s: Under whom did Andhra's Dharmakirti, who taught at Nalanda, study?
x: Dharmakirti studied under Dharmapala of Kanchi, the head of Nalanda (not the Pala king Dharmapala).

s: Shantarakshita of Nalanda founded which monastery in Tibet?
x: Shantarakshita of Nalanda founded the Samye monastery in Tibet.

s: With which mahavihara was Sakya Sri Bhadra, who took Tantric Buddhism to Tibet, associated?
x: Sakya Sri Bhadra belonged to Jagaddala. Atisha was from Vikramashila and Shantarakshita from Nalanda.

s: Who was the head of Nalanda in Harsha's time?
x: Shilabhadra headed Nalanda in Harsha's time.

s: With which mahavihara was Atisha Dipankara Srijnana, who went to Tibet in the eleventh century, associated?
x: Atisha Dipankara Srijnana of Vikramashila went to Tibet in the 11th century and revived Buddhism there.

s: Of which region was Balaputradeva, who set up a monastery at Nalanda, the ruler?
x: Balaputradeva was a Shailendra ruler of Suvarnadvipa or Suvarnabhumi. His envoy requested Devapala to grant five villages for maintaining the monastery at Nalanda.

s:
Consider the following statements about Balaputradeva:
1. He was a Shailendra ruler of Suvarnadvipa.
2. His envoy obtained five villages for his Nalanda monastery from Dharmapala.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Balaputradeva was the Shailendra ruler of Suvarnadvipa. The five villages were granted by Devapala, not Dharmapala.

s: Who was the last Sena ruler, whose court poet was Jayadeva and who was ousted by Bakhtiyar Khilji?
x: Lakshmanasena was the last Sena ruler; Jayadeva was at his court and he was ousted by Bakhtiyar Khilji.

s: Who founded the Sena dynasty of Bengal?
x: Samantasena, from Karnataka and a Pala feudatory in Rarh, founded the Sena line. Vijayasena founded independent Sena rule.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The scholar king Ballalasena wrote Danasagara and Adbhutasagara. Jayadeva was Lakshmanasena's poet, and Lakshmanasena was ousted by Bakhtiyar Khilji.

s: Who founded independent Sena rule in Bengal?
x: Samantasena founded the line as a Pala feudatory; Vijayasena made Sena rule independent.

s: In the time of Harsha, of which tradition was Valabhi a centre?
x: Valabhi was a Hinayana centre in Harsha's time, distinct from the Pala Mahaviharas.

s: Taxila, the odd one out among early medieval centres of learning, was the capital of which region?
x: Taxila was an early Buddhist centre and the capital of Gandhara, in present Rawalpindi district of Pakistan.

s: Which of the following studied at Taxila?
x: Taxila's students included Chanakya, Chandragupta Maurya, Charaka and Jivaka. Atisha, Shilabhadra and Dharmakirti belong to the Pala-era mahaviharas.

s: Which of the following was NOT a mahavihara of the Pala period?
x: Somapura, Jagaddala and Vikramashila were Pala mahaviharas; Valabhi was a Hinayana centre in western India in Harsha's time.

s: How did Gopala, the founder of the Pala dynasty, come to power?
o: Defeating the Sena ruler of Bengal
Inheritance from the later Guptas of Magadha
Election by notables to end matsyanyaya
x: Gopala was elected by regional notables in the mid-eighth century to end matsyanyaya, a period of anarchy.

s: The Pala founder Gopala displaced the Khadgas of which region?
x: Gopala displaced the later Guptas in Magadha and the Khadgas in eastern Bengal, and built Odantapuri.

s: Which inscription records the election of Gopala as king?
x: The Khalimpur inscription of Dharmapala records Gopala's election. The Nalanda copper plate records Devapala's grant of five villages.

s: Gopala was elected by the notables to end a state of anarchy. What was it called?
x: Gopala was elected in the mid-8th century to end matsyanyaya, the 'law of the jungle'. The Kaivarta revolt came under Ramapala.

s: Near which place was Dharmapala defeated by Nagabhata II?
x: Dharmapala (c. 770-810) was defeated by Dhruva and by Nagabhata II near Monghyr.

s: Which Pala ruler is associated with the revival of Pala power and was defeated by Rajendra Chola?
x: Mahipala I, whose reign is placed around c. 977–1027, revived Pala power and was defeated by Rajendra Chola.

s: In the reign of which Pala ruler did the Kaivarta revolt take place?
x: Ramapala (c. 1072-1126), the last strong Pala ruler, faced the Kaivarta revolt and is associated with Jagaddala.

s:
Consider the following statements about the grant to Balaputradeva's monastery at Nalanda:
1. The five villages were granted by Devapala.
2. The grant is recorded in the Nalanda copper plate.
3. The grant was made by Dharmapala, founder of Vikramashila.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Devapala granted the five villages, as the Nalanda copper plate records. Dharmapala founded Vikramashila but did not make this grant.

s: Which Pala ruler installed Chakrayudha on the throne of Kannauj?
x: Dharmapala installed Chakrayudha at Kannauj. Devapala is known for the Nalanda grant and Mahipala I for reviving Pala power.

s: Besides Nagabhata II, the Pala king Dharmapala was also defeated by which Rashtrakuta ruler?
x: Dharmapala was defeated by Dhruva and by Nagabhata II near Monghyr.

s: Which Pala ruler founded both Vikramashila and Somapura?
x: Dharmapala founded Vikramashila and Somapura; Gopala built Odantapuri and Nalanda was founded by Kumaragupta I.

s: Who founded the Jagaddala Mahavihara?
x: Jagaddala in Varendra was founded by Ramapala, the last strong Pala ruler. Gopala built Odantapuri and Dharmapala Vikramashila.

s: On which material were the illustrated Buddhist manuscripts of the Pala period written?
x: Pala art includes bronze and black-stone sculpture and illustrated palm-leaf Buddhist manuscripts.

s: Who were Dhiman and his son Vitapala of the Pala period, mentioned by Taranatha?
x: Dhiman and his son Vitapala were noted artists of Pala art, as recorded by Taranatha.

s: Who wrote Ramacharita, a work dealing with Ramapala and the Kaivarta peasant revolt?
x: Ramacharita was written by Sandhyakar Nandi and deals with Ramapala and the Kaivarta peasant revolt.

s: In which materials was Pala sculpture chiefly made?
x: Pala sculpture is known for bronze and black-stone (basalt) images.

s: Where is the grand-scale Pala terracotta decoration best seen?
x: Somapura shows Pala terracotta on a grand scale; Vikramashila has terracotta wall panels.

s: Sandhyakar Nandi's Ramacharita deals with which Pala ruler?
x: Ramacharita by Sandhyakar Nandi deals with Ramapala and the Kaivarta peasant revolt.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kannauj around 916 CE — Mahipala I defeated Indra III
Bundelkhand campaign — Govinda III defeated Nagabhata II
Early ninth-century Kannauj — Nagabhata II defeated Chakrayudha
x: Around 916 CE, Indra III defeated Mahipala I and sacked Kannauj. The other three pairs correctly identify the campaigns and victors.

s: The Pratihara king Vatsaraja, after taking Kannauj and defeating Dharmapala, was defeated by which Rashtrakuta ruler?
x: Vatsaraja took Kannauj and defeated Dharmapala but was later defeated by the Rashtrakuta Dhruva, marking the beginning of the tripartite struggle.

s: Near which place did the Pratihara king Nagabhata II defeat the Pala ruler Dharmapala?
x: Nagabhata II ousted Chakrayudha, defeated Dharmapala near Monghyr and made Kannauj the Pratihara capital.

s: Which Pratihara ruler came immediately after Vatsaraja?
x: The order is Vatsaraja, Nagabhata II, Mihira Bhoja, Mahendrapala I and Mahipala, so Nagabhata II followed Vatsaraja.

s: Which Rashtrakuta ruler defeated the Pratihara king Nagabhata II?
x: Nagabhata II was defeated by Govinda III, while his predecessor Vatsaraja lost to Dhruva.

s: Which Pratihara ruler bore the title 'Maharajadhiraja of Aryavarta'?
x: Mahendrapala I (c. 885–910) was styled Maharajadhiraja of Aryavarta and patronised Rajashekhara.

s: Mihira Bhoja was the grandson of Nagabhata II. Who was his father?
x: Mihira Bhoja was the son of Ramabhadra and therefore the grandson of Nagabhata II.

s: Mihir Bhoja captured Kannauj around which year?
x: Mihir Bhoja captured Kannauj around 836 AD and made it the Pratihara capital. 629 AD relates to Hiuen Tsang's journey.

s: Which ruler of Kashmir checked the expansion of the Pratihara king Mihira Bhoja?
x: Mihira Bhoja's expansion was checked by Sankaravarman of Kashmir, along with the Rashtrakuta Krishna II and the Pala Devapala.

s: Which of the following pairs about the Pratiharas is correctly matched?
x: Mihir Bhoja took the title Adivaraha. The Pratiharas first ruled from Ujjain, later from Kannauj, and Mihir Bhoja followed Vaishnavism.

s:
Consider the following statements about Mihira Bhoja:
1. He was the son of Ramabhadra.
2. He was the grandson of Nagabhata II.
3. His coins carry a Shaiva legend.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Mihira Bhoja was Ramabhadra's son and Nagabhata II's grandson. His coins carry the Vaishnava legend Adivaraha, not a Shaiva one.

s: Besides Adivaraha, which title did Mihira Bhoja bear?
x: Mihira Bhoja bore the titles Adivaraha and Prabhasa. Nripatunga and Viranarayana were Amoghavarsha I's, Prabhutavarsha Govinda III's.

s: Which title of Mihira Bhoja reflects his devotion to Vishnu and also appears as a legend on his coins?
x: Mihira Bhoja bore the title Adivaraha, reflecting his devotion to Vishnu; Adivaraha also appeared on his coins.

s: Rajashekhara was associated with the courts of which of the following rulers?
x: Rajashekhara was the court poet of Mahendrapala I and was also associated with the court of Mahipala I.

s: Which of the following works was NOT written by Rajashekhara?
x: Prabandhachintamani was written by Merutunga, whereas Kavyamimamsa, Karpuramanjari and Viddhasalabhanjika were works of Rajashekhara.

s: Who wrote the Prabandhachintamani?
x: Prabandhachintamani is Merutunga's work, not Rajashekhara's.

s: By what name did the Arab merchant Sulaiman (mid-9th century) refer to Mihira Bhoja?
x: Sulaiman called Mihira Bhoja 'Juzr' or 'Al-Juzr'; 'Baura' was Al-Masudi's name for him and Adivaraha was Bhoja's own title on his coins.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Arab traveller Sulaiman:
1. He praised the Pratihara cavalry.
2. He named Amoghavarsha I one of the four great kings of the world.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Sulaiman praised the Pratihara cavalry and named the Rashtrakuta Amoghavarsha I one of the four great kings of the world.

s: By what name did the Arab writer Al-Masudi call the Pratihara king?
x: Al-Masudi called the Pratihara king Baura; Juzr is Sulaiman's name for the kingdom, and Balhara was the Arab term for Rashtrakuta kings.

s: What does the term 'Pratihara' traditionally mean?
x: Pratihara means door-keeper. The dynasty claimed descent from Lakshmana, who was regarded as Rama's door-keeper brother.

s: According to the Agnikula legend in Prithviraj Raso, which group of dynasties was born from the fire-pit at Mount Abu?
x: The Agnikula legend associates the Pratiharas, Chaulukyas, Paramaras and Chauhans with birth from the fire-pit at Mount Abu.

s: Besides the Harshacharita, in which source are the Gurjaras first mentioned?
x: The Gurjaras are first mentioned in the Aihole inscription of Pulakesin II and Banabhatta's Harshacharita.

s: From whom did the Pratiharas claim descent?
x: 'Pratihara' means door-keeper; they claimed descent from Lakshmana, Rama's door-keeper brother.

s: Where was the early seat of the Gurjaras?
x: Bhinmal in Rajasthan was the early Gurjara seat; Ujjain and then Kannauj (Mahodaya) came later.

s: What was the capital of the Pratihara founder Nagabhata I?
x: Nagabhata I ruled from Ujjain (Avanti). Kannauj became the capital from Nagabhata II.

s: By what other name was Kannauj, the Pratihara capital from Nagabhata II's time, known?
x: Kannauj was also called Mahodaya; the Barah copper plate of Bhoja mentions a camp there.

s: Which copper plate of Mihira Bhoja mentions a camp (skandhavara) at Mahodaya?
x: The Barah copper plate of Bhoja mentions his camp at Mahodaya (Kannauj).

s: The Gurjara-Pratiharas were the main power that kept Arab rule confined to which region?
x: The Gurjara-Pratiharas were the principal power that helped keep Arab rule confined to Sindh.

s: Which ruler of Sindh was defeated and killed by Muhammad bin Qasim?
x: Muhammad bin Qasim led the Arab invasion of Sindh, defeated and killed Raja Dahir, and his conquest stayed largely within Sindh and Multan.

s: In which year did Muhammad bin Qasim take Sindh?
x: Muhammad bin Qasim took Sindh in 712, defeating and killing Raja Dahir.

s: The Gwalior inscription of Mihira Bhoja credits whom with repulsing the mleccha (Arab) army?
x: The Gwalior inscription says Nagabhata I repulsed the mleccha army.

s: In which year did Mahmud of Ghazni attack Kannauj, hastening the decline of the Gurjara-Pratiharas?
x: Mahmud of Ghazni attacked Kannauj in 1018, one of the blows (with Indra III's raid and the secession of feudatories) that weakened Pratihara power.

s: Which Rashtrakuta ruler looted Kannauj around 916, defeating the Pratihara Mahipala I?
x: Indra III raided Kannauj c. 916, defeating Mahipala I.

s: Which breakaway Pratihara feudatory is associated with Khajuraho?
x: The Chandelas of Khajuraho were among the feudatories that broke away as Pratihara power declined.

s: In which battle did the Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna III defeat the Cholas?
x: Krishna III defeated the Cholas at Takkolam (949 CE).

s: Who was the first Rashtrakuta ruler to march into northern India?
x: Dhruva was the first Rashtrakuta ruler to move north; he defeated Vatsaraja and Dharmapala.

s: Which one of the following was a military achievement of Govinda III?
o: Sacking Kannauj in the reign of Indra III
Defeating Nagabhata II and Dharmapala and reaching the Himalayas
x: Govinda III defeated Nagabhata II and Dharmapala and is said in the Sanjan plates to have reached the Himalayas.

s:
Consider the following statements about the order of Rashtrakuta rulers:
1. Dantidurga ruled from 753 to 756.
2. Dhruva ruled before Govinda III.
3. Amoghavarsha I ruled before Govinda III.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The order is Dantidurga (753-756), Dhruva (780-793), Govinda III (793-814) and Amoghavarsha I (814-878). Amoghavarsha I came after Govinda III.

s: Amoghavarsha I is particularly associated with which of the following combinations?
x: Amoghavarsha I built Manyakheta, was associated with Kavirajamarga, and is described as a Jain ruler or patron.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Amoghavarsha I was born in 800 AD.
Amoghavarsha I was born in a military camp.
Amoghavarsha I was born at Manyakheta.
Amoghavarsha I was born at Shribhavan.
x: Option C is incorrect: Amoghavarsha I was born in 800 CE at Shribhavan, near the Narmada, in a military camp, not at Manyakheta. Manyakheta was the Rashtrakuta capital he built.

s: Which record describes Govinda III's campaign up to the Himalayas?
x: The Sanjan and Radhanpur plates record Govinda III's northern campaign.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Dhruva – first Rashtrakuta to go north
Krishna III – Kailasa temple at Ellora
x: The Kailasa temple at Ellora was built by Krishna I, not Krishna III, who won at Takkolam.

s: In which cave at Ellora is the Kailasa temple built by Krishna I?
x: The monolithic Kailasa (Kailashnatha) temple of Krishna I is Ellora Cave 16.

s: Kavirajamarga, the earliest work on Kannada poetics, is associated with which Rashtrakuta ruler?
x: Kavirajamarga (c. 850) is associated with Amoghavarsha I and is the earliest work on Kannada poetics.

s: Who wrote the Sanskrit Adipurana?
x: Jinasena wrote a Sanskrit Adipurana, while Pampa wrote a Kannada Adipurana on the life of Rishabhadeva.

s: The Kannada ‘Ratnatraya’ traditionally refers to which group?
x: The Kannada Ratnatraya consisted of Pampa, Ponna and Ranna, the three celebrated Kannada poets associated with major royal patrons.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Nalachampu was written by Trivikrama Bhatta. Halayudha was the author of Kavirahasya.

s: By what other name is Pampa's Kannada epic Vikramarjuna Vijaya known?
x: Vikramarjuna Vijaya is also called Pampa Bharata; in it Pampa modelled Arjuna on his patron Arikesari II.

s: Who wrote the Ganitasarasangraha, a Sanskrit work on mathematics?
x: Ganitasarasangraha is by Mahaviracharya.

s:
Consider the following statements about Rashtrakuta-era literature:
1. Kavirajamarga by Amoghavarsha I is in Kannada.
2. Prashnottara Ratnamalika is in Sanskrit.
3. Nalachampu was written by Halayudha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Kavirajamarga is in Kannada and Prashnottara Ratnamalika in Sanskrit. Nalachampu is by Trivikrama Bhatta; Halayudha wrote Kavirahasya.

s: Who among the following was the Telugu-origin Adikavi of Kannada?
x: Pampa, of Telugu origin and brother of Jinavallabha, is the Adikavi of Kannada; he wrote Vikramarjuna Vijaya.

s: In which language did Pampa write the Vikramarjuna Vijaya?
x: Vikramarjuna Vijaya (Pampa Bharata) is a Kannada version of the Mahabharata, though Pampa was of Telugu origin.

s: Pampa's Kannada Adipurana describes the life of whom?
x: Pampa's Kannada Adipurana is on the life of Rishabhadeva, the first Jain Tirthankara.

s: Who wrote the Prashnottara Ratnamalika?
x: The Sanskrit Jain text Prashnottara Ratnamalika is credited to Amoghavarsha I.

s: Who patronised the Kannada poet Ponna?
x: Ponna was patronised by the Rashtrakuta Krishna III; Pampa was patronised by Arikesari II and Ranna by Tailapa II.

s: Which of the following poet – patron pairs is correctly matched?
x: Pampa was patronised by Arikesari II of Vemulavada. Ponna's patron was Krishna III and Ranna's Tailapa II.

s: Who wrote the Gadayuddha?
x: Ranna, patronised by Tailapa II, wrote Gadayuddha.

s: Who was the patron of the Kannada poet Ranna, author of Gadayuddha?
x: Ranna was patronised by the Western Chalukya Tailapa II.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Vemulavada Chalukyas:
1. They ruled from the present Karimnagar region as feudatories of the Rashtrakutas.
2. They were strong patrons of Jainism.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Vemulavada Chalukyas of Karimnagar were Rashtrakuta feudatories and patrons of Jain poets like Pampa and Somadeva Suri.

s: Which inscription of Jinavallabha contains early Telugu verses?
x: Jinavallabha, Pampa's brother, issued the Kurkyala inscription with early Telugu verses.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Hiranyagarbha ritual – Performed by Dantidurga at Ujjayini
Kavirajamarga – Sanskrit treatise by Krishna I
x: Dantidurga performed the Hiranyagarbha at Ujjayini. Kailasa is a Shaiva rock-cut monument, Jinasena wrote the Adipurana, and Kavirajamarga is Amoghavarsha I's Kannada work.

s: Which ritual did Dantidurga perform at Ujjayini?
x: Dantidurga performed the Hiranyagarbha ritual at Ujjayini (Ujjain).

s: Dantidurga overthrew which Badami Chalukya ruler?
x: Dantidurga, a former Chalukya feudatory, overthrew Kirtivarman II of Badami.

s: In which cave at Ellora is Dantidurga's inscription found?
x: Dantidurga's inscription is in Ellora's Dashavatara cave; the Kailasa temple (Cave 16) was built later by Krishna I.

s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler was a contemporary of the Rashtrakuta founder Dantidurga?
x: Dantidurga (753-756) was a contemporary of Eastern Chalukya Vijayaditya I.

s: Who built Manyakheta, the Rashtrakuta capital?
x: Amoghavarsha I built Manyakheta; the early Rashtrakuta seat had been in the Elapura (Ellora) region.

s: In which present-day state is Manyakheta, also known as Malkhed, located?
x: Manyakheta or Malkhed is in Karnataka and was built by Amoghavarsha I.

s: What was the early seat of the Rashtrakutas?
x: Elapura (Ellora) was the early seat; Manyakheta was built later by Amoghavarsha I.

s: In which architectural style is the Kailasa temple at Ellora built?
x: The Kailasa temple is a Shaiva temple in the Dravidian style, recalling Mount Kailasa.

s: Which title did the Rashtrakuta Amoghavarsha I take after his victory at Vingavalli?
x: Amoghavarsha I won at Vingavalli and took the title Viranarayana.

s: 'Nripatunga' was a title of which Rashtrakuta ruler?
x: Nripatunga and Viranarayana were titles of Amoghavarsha I; Prabhutavarsha was associated with Govinda III.

s: For whom did Arab writers use the term 'Balhara'?
o: The Chola kings who ruled at Takkolam
x: Balhara is the Arab form associated with Vallabharaja and was used generally for Rashtrakuta kings. Al-Masudi was a contemporary source for this usage.

s: 'Prabhutavarsha' was a title of which Rashtrakuta ruler?
x: Prabhutavarsha was Govinda III's title; Nripatunga and Viranarayana were Amoghavarsha I's.

s: Which ruler was visited by Sulaiman, who regarded him as one of the four great kings of the world?
x: Sulaiman visited the court of Amoghavarsha I and considered him one of the four great kings of the world.

s: Which Arab writer called the Balhara the 'king of kings'?
x: Ibn Khurdadhbih called the Balhara the greatest king of India, 'king of kings'.

s: In which year did the Arab traveller Sulaiman visit India in the reign of Amoghavarsha I?
x: Sulaiman's account dates to 851, in Amoghavarsha I's reign.

s: At the battle of Takkolam (949 CE), Krishna III defeated which Chola king?
x: At Takkolam in 949 CE, Krishna III defeated the Cholas under Parantaka I, and the Chola prince Rajaditya was killed.

s: Who led the Chola side at the Battle of Takkolam (949 CE)?
x: Rajaditya led the Cholas at Takkolam, where the Western Gangas and Vaidumbas fought on the Rashtrakuta side.

s: At Takkolam (949 CE), Krishna III was helped by the Western Gangas and which other power?
x: Krishna III fought at Takkolam with the Western Gangas and the Vaidumbas against the Cholas of Parantaka I.

s: For about how long did the Rashtrakuta–Vengi conflict continue?
x: The Rashtrakuta–Vengi conflict lasted about 200 years, with repeated struggles against the Eastern Chalukyas.

s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler is credited with fighting 108 battles against the Rashtrakuta forces?
x: Vijayaditya II of Vengi is credited with fighting 108 battles against the Rashtrakutas.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Eastern Chalukya ruler Vijayaditya II:
1. He is associated with building 108 Shiva temples.
2. He is linked with the naming of Vijayawada.
3. He composed the Kavirajamarga in Kannada.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Vijayaditya II is associated with 108 Shiva temples and the naming of Vijayawada. Kavirajamarga was written by the Rashtrakuta Amoghavarsha I.

s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler defeated the Rashtrakuta Krishna II?
x: Gunaga Vijayaditya III beat Krishna II. Vijayaditya II fought 108 battles and Vijayaditya I was Dantidurga's contemporary.

s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler gave his daughter Shila Mahadevi to Dhruva?
x: Defeated by Dhruva, Vishnuvardhana IV gave his daughter Shila Mahadevi to him.

s: Who overthrew the Rashtrakuta line around 973 CE?
x: After Paramara Siyaka II defeated Khottiga and sacked Manyakheta, Tailapa II of the Kalyani Chalukyas overthrew the Rashtrakuta line around 973 CE.

s: The Paramara Siyaka II defeated which Rashtrakuta ruler and sacked Manyakheta?
x: Siyaka II defeated Khottiga on the Narmada and sacked Manyakheta.

s: Which styles are combined in the Vesara synthesis associated with the Rashtrakutas?
x: The Rashtrakutas contributed to the Vesara synthesis, which combined Nagara and Dravida architectural features and became associated with the Deccan style.

s: The Kailasa temple (Cave 16) at Ellora was carved during the reign of which Rashtrakuta ruler?
x: It was carved under Krishna I (r. 756-773 CE). Dantidurga founded the dynasty, Amoghavarsha I built Manyakheta, and crediting Krishna III with it was the wrong pair in APPSC G1 2024.

s: The vimana (tower) of the Kailasa temple at Ellora is built in which style?
x: Kailasa has a three-tiered Dravida vimana, even though it stands in Nagara territory in Maharashtra.

s: The Kailasa temple at Ellora was carved top-down from a single cliff of which rock?
x: Kailasa is a monolithic temple carved top-down from a single basalt cliff.

s: Which of the following is the largest monolithic rock excavation in the world?
x: The Kailasa temple (Ellora Cave 16), carved top-down from one basalt cliff, is the largest monolithic rock excavation in the world.

s: To which deity is the Kailasa temple (Cave 16) at Ellora dedicated?
x: The Kailasa temple is dedicated to Shiva as the lord of Mount Kailasa.

s: The Kailasa temple at Ellora is which cave of the Ellora group?
x: The monolithic Kailasa temple is Cave 16; Cave 10 is the Buddhist chaitya.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Rashtrakuta king Krishna III?
o: He helped Danarnava kill the Eastern Chalukya ruler Ammaraja II
The killing of Ammaraja II took place in 970 CE
Vengi was seized after the killing of Ammaraja II
The Kailasa temple at Ellora was carved during his reign
x: Krishna III helped Danarnava kill Ammaraja II in 970 CE and seize Vengi. The Kailasa temple was carved under Krishna I, not Krishna III.

s: The Ellora caves are carved in which hills of Aurangabad district, Maharashtra?
x: Ellora lies in the Charanandri hills near the Elaganga river, on the ancient Ujjain-Deccan route; the caves were carved c. 600-1000 CE.

s: Which dynasty mainly carved the Hindu caves (13-29) at Ellora?
x: The Hindu caves at Ellora are mainly Rashtrakuta work; the Buddhist caves (c. 600-730 CE) are the earliest and the Jain caves the latest.

s: Which of the following Ellora cave – feature pairs is correctly matched?
o: Cave 10 – The only chaitya at Ellora
x: Cave 10 is the only chaitya at Ellora. Cave 14 is Ravan ki Khai, Cave 16 is Kailasa and Cave 32 is Indra Sabha.

s: How many caves make up the Ellora group, and how are they divided among the three faiths?
x: Ellora has 34 caves (APPSC-GS 2024): Buddhist 12 (Caves 1-12), Hindu 17 (Caves 13-29) and Jain 5 (Caves 30-34). The 17-12 swap and the totals of 29 or 30 are wrong.

s: Which of the following Ellora caves is the latest in date?
x: The order is Dumar Lena (Cave 29, 6th century) → Ravan ki Khai (14) → Dashavatara (15) → Kailasa (16, Krishna I), so Kailasa is the latest of the four. (The old explanation put Ravan ki Khai before Dumar Lena.)

s: India and Jordan signed a twinning agreement concerning which pair of UNESCO sites?
x: The twinning agreement signed by India and Jordan concerned Petra and Ellora, both UNESCO sites.

s: The Indra Sabha (Cave 32) at Ellora belongs to which group?
x: Indra Sabha, Cave 32, is a Jain (Digambara) cave of the Jain group, caves 30-34.

s: Which group of caves is the earliest at Ellora?
x: The Buddhist caves (1-12) are the earliest, c. 600-730 CE, before the Rashtrakutas; the Jain caves are the latest.

s:
Arrange the following cave groups of Ellora in chronological order of their excavation:
1. Jain caves
2. Buddhist caves
3. Hindu caves
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: The Buddhist caves (1-12) are the earliest, the Hindu caves (13-29) mainly Rashtrakuta, and the Jain caves (30-34) the latest, of the 9th-10th century.

s: Which cave at Ellora carries the inscription of the Rashtrakuta ruler Dantidurga?
x: Dantidurga's inscription is in the Dashavatara cave (Cave 15), which came before the Kailasa cave of Krishna I.

s: Near which river are the Ellora caves located?
x: The Ellora caves lie in the Charanandri hills near the Elaganga river.

s: What is the local name of the Ellora caves?
x: Ellora is known locally as Verul Leni.

s: To which Jain sect does the Indra Sabha (Cave 32) at Ellora belong?
x: Indra Sabha, Cave 32, is a Digambara Jain cave.

s: Many historians date the main Elephanta cave with the Trimurti to which dynasty?
x: Though an MPPSC key credited it to the Rashtrakutas, many historians date the main Elephanta cave to the 6th-century Kalachuris.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Elephanta caves:
1. They form an island cave complex near Mumbai.
2. Their masterpiece is the three-headed Shiva known as Trimurti.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Elephanta is an island cave complex near Mumbai, and its masterpiece is the Trimurti (Maheshamurti).

s: Which faith reached its zenith of Rashtrakuta patronage under Amoghavarsha I?
x: Jainism reached a high point under Amoghavarsha I, who was a devout Jain and is described as having renounced the throne.

s: The early Rashtrakuta rulers were staunch followers of which faith?
x: Early Rashtrakuta rulers were staunch Shaivas, though Vaishnavism and Buddhism also received patronage without persecution.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Rashtrakuta religious policy?
o: The early rulers were staunch Shaivas
Jainism reached its peak under Amoghavarsha I
Buddhists were persecuted by the rulers
Arab merchants were allowed to build mosques
x: Vaishnavism and Buddhism received royal patronage and there was no persecution.

s: Who among the following travellers ranked the Rashtrakuta king among the four great kings of the world?
x: Sulaiman, who visited during the reign of Amoghavarsha I, ranked the Rashtrakuta king among the four great kings along with the Caliph, the Chinese emperor and the Byzantine emperor.

s: During whose reign did the Arab traveller Al-Masudi visit the Rashtrakuta kingdom (c. 915-16 CE)?
x: Al-Masudi came c. 915-16 CE under Indra III and described the Balhara as having many Arab/Muslim subjects.

s: The Arab title 'Balhara' for the Rashtrakuta king is derived from which title?
x: Balhara is the Arabic form of the Rashtrakuta title Vallabha (Vallabharaja).

s: Which of the following traveller – Rashtrakuta king pairs is correctly matched?
x: Sulaiman wrote in the reign of Amoghavarsha I; Al-Masudi visited c. 915-16 CE under Indra III.

s: Who headed the Vishaya in Rashtrakuta administration?
x: The Vishaya was headed by the Vishayapati; the Rashtra by the Rashtrapati, the Bhukti by the Bhogapati and the Grama by the Gramakuta or gavunda.

s: What were the hereditary local officers of the nadu who helped in revenue collection called in Rashtrakuta administration?
x: Nad-gavundas were hereditary local officers of the nadu who assisted in revenue collection.

s: Who headed the Rashtra (province) in Rashtrakuta administration?
x: The Rashtra was under the Rashtrapati; the Vishaya under the Vishayapati, the Bhukti under the Bhogapati and the Grama under the Gramakuta.

s: Which unit was headed by the Bhogapati in Rashtrakuta administration?
x: The Bhukti, a unit smaller than the Vishaya, was headed by the Bhogapati.

s: Who headed the village (grama) in Rashtrakuta administration?
x: The grama (village) was under the Gramakuta or gavunda; the Rashtrapati, Vishayapati and Bhogapati headed larger units.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Rashtrakuta trade?
o: Horses were imported by sea from Arabia.
Cambay, Thana and Sopara were western ports connected with this trade.
Textiles were among the goods exported.
Arab merchants were barred from settling in the western ports.
x: Arab merchants settled peacefully in the western ports, so the statement that they were barred is false; the horse imports, textile exports and the listed ports are correct.

s: From where did the Rashtrakutas import horses by sea?
x: Horses were imported by sea from Arabia, while textiles were exported.

s: Under pressure from which powers did the Rashtrakutas decline by the late tenth century?
x: The Rashtrakutas declined by the late tenth century under Chalukya-Chola pressure.

s: The Rashtrakuta era raised which language to a classical literary medium?
x: The Rashtrakuta era raised Kannada to a classical medium.

s: In which year was Vatapi fortified by Pulakesin I, according to the Badami cliff inscription?
x: Pulakesin I fortified Vatapi, as recorded in the Badami cliff inscription dated to 543 CE.

s: Vatapi, the Badami Chalukya capital, is in which district of Karnataka?
x: Vatapi is modern Badami in Bagalkot district, set in sandstone hills around Agastya lake.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Vatapi was the capital of the Badami Chalukyas.
The Badami Chalukyas ruled mainly in the Deccan and Southern India.
Kanchi was the capital of the Badami Chalukyas.
Vatapi is identified with present-day Badami in Bagalkot, Karnataka.
x: Option C is incorrect: Kanchi was the Pallava capital. The Badami Chalukyas ruled from Vatapi, present-day Badami in Bagalkot district, Karnataka, and their power lay in the Deccan and South India.

s: The Badami Chalukyas ruled approximately during which period?
x: The Badami (Vatapi) Chalukyas ruled from about 543 CE, under Pulakeshin I, to 753 CE, when Dantidurga overthrew Kirtivarman II. The other ranges are reigns of single kings: Vikramaditya I, Pulakeshin II and Kirtivarman II.

s: Which Pallava king captured and destroyed Vatapi in 642 CE and took the title Vatapikonda?
x: The Pallava Narasimhavarman I destroyed Vatapi in 642 CE and took the title Vatapikonda; Chalukya power was later restored by Vikramaditya I.

s: Pulakesin II exchanged embassies with which Persian king?
x: Pulakesin II exchanged embassies with the Persian king Khusrau II; the Ajanta Cave 1 painting once read as this embassy is now doubted.

s: Which one of the following inscriptions records the appointment of Kubja Vishnuvardhana as viceroy of Vengi?
x: The Satara inscription of 617 CE records Pulakesin II's appointment of his brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana as viceroy of Vengi.

s: After defeating whom did Pulakesin II assume the title Paramesvara?
x: Pulakesin II took the title Paramesvara after defeating Harsha, not Mahendravarman I; his other titles included Dakshinapatheshwara, Satyashraya and Prithvivallabha.

s: Which inscription of 630 CE does not mention Harsha among the defeated enemies of Pulakeshin II?
x: The Lohnara inscription of 630 CE lists enemies defeated by Pulakeshin II but does not include Harsha. The Aihole inscription of 634 CE does record his victory over Harsha.

s: Who is credited with the Chinese account of China–India relations under the Chalukyas?
x: The account of China–India relations under the Chalukyas is credited to Ma Twan-lin, also rendered in some references as Matwalin. Hiuen Tsang visited Pulakesin II's kingdom and praised him in comparison with Harsha and Narasimhavarman.

s: Which was the capital of the Eastern Chalukyas, who became independent at Vengi in 624 CE?
x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana made Vengi independent in 624 CE, founding the Eastern Chalukyas with their capital at Pithapuram.

s: Who among the following is credited with the first gold coins of South India?
x: Pulakesin II is credited with the first South Indian gold coins.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Narmada – Site of Pulakeshin II's conflict with Harsha
x: The Narmada was where Pulakeshin II checked Harsha. Badami was the Chalukya capital, Kanchi the Pallava capital and Tanjore the Chola capital.

s:
Consider the following statements about Pulakesin II's eastern campaign:
1. He conquered Kosala and Kalinga before marching to Vengi.
2. After taking Vengi he defeated the Durjayas and then turned against the Pallava Mahendravarman I.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: Pulakesin II conquered Kosala and Kalinga, marched to Vengi, defeated the Durjayas and then fought the Pallava Mahendravarman I. In 617 the Satara inscription records his brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana as viceroy of Vengi.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Ruler)
A. Kushanas
B. Pulakesin II
C. Harshavardhana
D. Samudragupta
List-II (Title)
1. Kaviraja
2. Devaputra
3. Dakshinapatheshwara
4. Sakalottarapathanatha
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: The Kushanas were Devaputra, Pulakesin II Dakshinapatheshwara (Lord of the Deccan), Harsha Sakalottarapathanatha and Samudragupta Kaviraja.

s: Which Chinese traveller visited the kingdom of Pulakesin II and praised him?
x: Hiuen Tsang visited the Chalukya kingdom and praised Pulakesin II along with Harsha and Narasimhavarman.

s: In which year did Vengi become independent under the Eastern Chalukyas?
x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana was viceroy of Vengi in 617 CE (Satara inscription); Vengi became independent in 624 CE.

s: In the Aihole inscription, Kirtivarman I is called 'the night of doom' to which powers?
x: Kirtivarman I is described as the ‘night of doom’ to the Nalas, Mauryas and Kadambas.

s: The Aihole inscription, composed by Ravikirti, is written in which language?
x: The Aihole inscription is in Sanskrit (not Prakrit), in the Southern Brahmi script, and is the key source for Pulakeshin II.

s: The Aihole inscription of Pulakesin II (634-35 CE) is engraved on which temple?
x: The Aihole prasasti by Ravikirti is on the Meguti Jain temple at Aihole; the Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal was built by Lokamahadevi.

s: According to the Aihole inscription, Pulakesin II defeated Harsha on the banks of which river?
x: The Aihole inscription says Pulakesin II defeated Harsha at the Narmada; it also records victories over Kosala, Kalinga and the Pallavas.

s: With whom did Ravikirti, author of the Aihole inscription, compare his fame?
x: Ravikirti names Kalidasa and Bharavi in the Aihole inscription, claiming to equal their fame.

s: Ravikirti, the composer of the Aihole inscription, followed which faith?
x: Ravikirti was a Jain court poet of Pulakesin II, and the inscription is on the Meguti Jain temple.

s: Pishtapura, listed among the victories of Pulakesin II in the Aihole inscription, is which modern place?
x: The Aihole inscription lists Kosala, Kalinga and Pishtapura (Pithapuram) among the victories.

s: Who is the author of the Aihole inscription of Pulakesin II?
x: The Aihole inscription (634-35 CE) was composed by Ravikirti, the Jain court poet of Pulakesin II.

s: In which year was the Aihole inscription of Pulakesin II composed?
x: The Aihole inscription is dated 634-35 CE (Saka era); 543 CE is the Badami cliff inscription and 642 CE the fall of Vatapi.

s: In which script is the Aihole inscription of Ravikirti written?
x: The Aihole inscription is a Sanskrit prasasti in the Southern Brahmi script.

s: The Maruturu and Kopparam inscriptions associate Pulakesin II with which achievement in Andhra?
o: Foundation of the Eastern Chalukya kingdom at Pithapuram
Defeat of Harsha on the banks of the Godavari
Defeat of the Pallava ruler Mahendravarman I and control over the land between the Krishna and Godavari
Appointment of Kubja Vishnuvardhana as governor of Kalinga
x: The Maruturu and Kopparam inscriptions record Pulakesin II's defeat of Mahendravarman I and his securing of the territory between the Krishna and Godavari rivers.

s: What name did Dandin give to Vengi?
x: The literary author Dandin called Vengi ‘Andhra Nagaram’.

s: Whose Pune copper plates contain the first epigraphic reference to Guntur as Kumturu?
x: The Pune copper plates of Eastern Chalukya Vishnuvardhana II, dated 669 CE, contain the first epigraphic reference to Guntur as Kumturu.

s: Which inscription of Pulakesin II refers to Mangalagiri as 'Mangalapura'?
x: The Marturu (Maruturu) inscription of Pulakesin II calls Mangalagiri 'Mangalapura' (APPSC-GS 2018 key), not Kopparam. The Aihole inscription is Ravikirti's prasasti and the Satara inscription records Kubja Vishnuvardhana's appointment to Vengi.

s: Which of the following is an inscription of Kubja Vishnuvardhana in Andhra?
x: Chipurupalli is among Kubja Vishnuvardhana's inscriptions; Maruturu, Aihole and Lohnara belong to Pulakesin II.

s: Who overthrew Kirtivarman II, the last Badami Chalukya ruler?
x: Dantidurga overthrew Kirtivarman II and founded the Rashtrakuta power around 753-757 CE.

s: With which ruler are the earliest rock-cut caves at Badami associated?
x: Mangalesha is associated with the earliest rock-cut caves at Badami.

s: Which ruler took Kanchi three times but spared the city and is associated with the Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal?
x: Vikramaditya II took Kanchi three times but spared it. His queen Lokamahadevi built the Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Badami Chalukya rulers:
1. Pulakesin I ruled before Kirtivarman I.
2. Mangalesha ruled before Kirtivarman I.
3. Vikramaditya I ruled after Mangalesha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The order is Pulakesin I, Kirtivarman I, Mangalesha (regent) and Vikramaditya I. Mangalesha came after Kirtivarman I, so statement 2 is wrong.

s: Which Badami Chalukya ruler annexed the Kadambas, the Gangas and the Mauryas of Konkan?
x: Kirtivarman I annexed the Kadambas, Gangas and Mauryas of Konkan; Pulakesin I performed the Ashvamedha and Pulakesin II took the title Dakshinapatheshwara.

s: With which claim of the Chalukya kings were their Vajapeya and Hiranyagarbha sacrifices connected?
x: The Vajapeya and Hiranyagarbha sacrifices were used by Chalukya kings to claim Kshatriya status.

s: Which Badami Chalukya ruler, the real founder of the dynasty, performed the Ashvamedha sacrifice?
x: Pulakesin I (543-566) was the real founder; he performed the Ashvamedha and walled Vatapi.

s: Which inscription records the Bahusuvarna-Agnishtoma sacrifice of Kirtivarman I?
x: The Mahakuta pillar records Kirtivarman I's Bahusuvarna-Agnishtoma sacrifice.

s: Who was the last ruler of the Badami Chalukya dynasty?
x: Kirtivarman II (746-753) was the last Badami Chalukya ruler, overthrown by Dantidurga.

s: Which Badami Chalukya ruler revived Chalukya power after the Pallava occupation of Vatapi?
x: Vikramaditya I (655-680) revived Chalukya power after the Pallavas had held Vatapi.

s: Which queen of Vikramaditya II built the Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal?
x: Lokamahadevi, queen of Vikramaditya II, built the Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal.

s: Why did Mangalesha become ruler after the death of Kirtivarman I?
o: He was the eldest son of Kirtivarman I.
He was appointed by the Pallava king.
He succeeded after defeating Vikramaditya II.
He ruled as regent because Kirtivarman I had left minor sons.
x: Kirtivarman I left minor sons, so his brother Mangalesha governed as regent.

s: Where did Pulakesin II defeat and kill Mangalesha?
x: After exile, Pulakesin II attacked and killed Mangalesha at Elapattu-Simbige in the Bana territory around 609-10 CE.

s: The Aihole inscription recording the Narmada victory of Pulakesin II belongs to which year?
x: The Aihole record is dated 634 CE. It was composed by Ravikirti and records the defeat of Harsha.

s: Which inscription, composed by Ravikirti, records the conflict between Pulakesin II and Harsha?
x: The Aihole inscription by Ravikirti, together with Hiuen Tsang's account, is the source for the Pulakesin II-Harsha conflict; the Kailasanatha inscription is not.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Chalukya-Harsha conflict:
1. It is known from the Aihole inscription and Hiuen Tsang.
2. It is recorded in the Kailasanatha inscription.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Narmada victory is known from the Aihole inscription and Hiuen Tsang, not the Kailasanatha inscription.

s: In which year did Pulakesin II stop Harsha's southward march on the Narmada?
x: The battle of the Narmada is dated 618 CE; the Aihole inscription that records it is of 634 CE.

s: Pulakesin II assumed the title 'Paramesvara' after his conflict with Harsha. By which other title was he known?
x: Pulakesin II was styled Dakshinapatheshwara, meaning lord of the south, in opposition to Harsha’s title Uttarapatheshwara.

s: Pulakesin II's title Dakshinapatheshwara was set against which title of Harsha?
x: Pulakesin II was Dakshinapatheshwara, lord of the south, against Harsha's Uttarapatheshwara.

s: Up to which place did Pulakesin II advance in the first round of the Chalukya-Pallava conflict?
x: In the first round Pulakesin II advanced to Kanchi and won territory in the Krishna-Godavari region; in the second round Narasimhavarman I defeated him and took Vatapi.

s: Which of the following Chalukya-Pallava rounds is NOT correctly matched with its rulers?
o: First round – Pulakesin II and Narasimhavarman I
Second round – Pulakesin II and Narasimhavarman I
Third round – Vikramaditya I and the Pallavas
Fourth round – Vikramaditya II and Nandivarman II
x: The first round was fought between Pulakesin II and Mahendravarman I; Narasimhavarman I was his opponent in the second round.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Vikramaditya II — Kanchi taken three times and spared
Nandivarman II — Overthrow of the Rashtrakutas
x: C is wrong: Nandivarman II was the Pallava ruler whose Kanchi Vikramaditya II took three times and spared; he did not overthrow the Rashtrakutas. It was the Rashtrakutas (under Dantidurga) who replaced the Chalukyas. The other three pairs are correct.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched (Chalukya-Pallava conflict)?
o: Pallava occupation of Vatapi – about 13 years
Power that replaced the Badami Chalukyas – Cholas
Vikramaditya I – recovered Vatapi c. 655 CE
x: The Chalukya-Pallava rivalry ended when the Rashtrakutas, not the Cholas, replaced the Chalukyas in the mid-eighth century; the other pairs are correct (642 to c. 655).

s: For about how many years did the Pallavas occupy Vatapi after 642 CE?
x: The Pallavas held Vatapi from 642 to c. 655, about 13 years, until Vikramaditya I recovered it.

s: Near which place was the Battle of Pullalur (c. 618-619 CE), whose victor is disputed, fought?
x: Pullalur was fought near Kanchi around 618-619; Pallava records credit Mahendravarman I and Chalukya records claim victory for Pulakesin II.

s: Who won the Battle of Manimangala (c. 642 CE)?
x: Narasimhavarman I defeated Pulakesin II at Manimangala, as also at Pariyala and Suramara.

s: Which Pallava general sacked Vatapi in 642 CE?
x: Narasimhavarman I took Vatapi in 642, and it was sacked by his general Paranjoti.

s: Who assumed the title 'Kanchiyamkonda'?
x: Vikramaditya II took the title Kanchiyamkonda after taking Kanchi during the reign of Nandivarman II.

s: Who assumed the title ‘Vatapikonda’?
x: Narasimhavarman I assumed the title Vatapikonda, meaning conqueror of Vatapi, after capturing the Chalukya capital.

s: Which pair of queens commissioned the Virupaksha and Mallikarjuna temples at Pattadakal?
x: Lokamahadevi and Trailokyamahadevi, queens of Vikramaditya II, commissioned the Virupaksha and Mallikarjuna temples at Pattadakal.

s: Which Badami Chalukya queen administered the kingdom after the death of her husband Chandraditya?
x: Vijaya Bhattarika, queen of Chandraditya, governed after his death, reflecting how the Badami Chalukyas often gave women high administrative posts.

s: Which Kalyani Chalukya princess governed Kisukad?
x: The Kalyani Chalukya princess Akkadevi governed Kisukad.

s: To which institution did Kumkumdevi, sister of Vikramaditya I, grant a village?
x: Kumkumdevi granted a village to a Jain monastery.

s: Whose queen was Vijayabhattarika, who issued land grants in her own name?
x: Vijayabhattarika (Vijaya-mahadevi) was the queen of Chandraditya; she governed and issued land grants in her own name.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Kalyani Chalukya princess Akkadevi governed Kisukad.
2. The Eastern Chalukya queens Ayyana Mahadevi and Chamakamba served as provincial governors.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Akkadevi governed Kisukad, but the Eastern Chalukya queens Ayyana Mahadevi and Chamakamba were temple builders, not governors.

s: Vikramaditya II occupied Kanchi around 740 CE during the reign of which Pallava king?
x: Vikramaditya II entered Kanchi c. 740 CE in Nandivarman II's reign, gifted gold to the Rajasimheshvara temple and left a Kannada inscription on a pillar.

s: In which language is the inscription that Vikramaditya II left on a pillar at Kanchi?
x: Vikramaditya II left a Kannada inscription on a pillar at Kanchi.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Vikramaditya II's occupation of Kanchi?
o: It took place in Nandivarman II's reign
He gave gold to the Rajasimheshvara temple
x: Vikramaditya II did not plunder Kanchi; he gave gold to the Rajasimheshvara (Kailasanatha) temple.

s: The Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal, built by Lokamahadevi, copies which temple of Kanchi?
x: Lokamahadevi's Virupaksha temple copies the Kailasanatha (Rajasimheshvara) temple of Kanchi, which Vikramaditya II saw when he entered Kanchi.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Badami Chalukya society and administration?
o: Agraharas were land grants made to Brahmins.
Vatapi and Aihole had no urban or trade role.
R.S. Sharma called their spread the 'proliferation of the feudal land grant system'.
x: Vatapi and Aihole were urban and trade centres, not purely religious ones, so that statement is false; the other three are correct.

s: The Renati Chodas of Rayalaseema were first feudatories of the early Pallavas. Whose feudatories did they later become?
x: The Renati Chodas were initially feudatories of the early Pallavas and subsequently of the Badami Chalukyas.

s: The Pallava–Chalukya wars stimulated the rise of which powers in Rayalaseema?
x: The wars stimulated political activity in Rayalaseema, including the rise of the Renati Chodas, Banas and Vaidumbas.

s: What does the eighth-century inscription in early Telugu script found at Pitikayagulla indicate?
o: The origin of the Rashtrakuta dynasty in Kanchi
The direct rule of Harsha in Rayalaseema
x: The Pitikayagulla inscription indicates post-Badami Chalukya influence in Rayalaseema and is written in early Telugu script.

s: Who ran the agraharas (Brahmin land grants) under the Badami Chalukyas?
x: Agraharas were Brahmin land grants run by mahajanas.

s:
Consider the following statements about Badami Chalukya administration:
1. The vishaya was a district under the vishayapati.
2. The Rashtrakutas were among its feudatories.
3. Vatapi and Aihole were urban and trade centres.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: vishaya under the vishayapati, Rashtrakutas among the feudatories, and Vatapi and Aihole as urban and trade centres.

s: Which temple is regarded as the oldest Saivite temple?
x: Parasurameswara Temple at Gudimallam, with its early Shiva linga, is regarded as the oldest Saivite temple. Arasavalli is a Surya temple and Hampi and Alampur temples are much later.

s: The Navabrahma temples of the Badami Chalukyas at Alampur stand on the banks of which river?
x: The Navabrahma group is a complex of nine Nagara temples on the Tungabhadra at Alampur, built by the Badami Chalukyas in the 7th-8th centuries.

s: Alampur is also known by which of the following names, and is associated with which religious centre?
o: Dakshina Gaya and the Kamakhya Shakti Peetha
Uttarapatha Kashi and the Bhramaramba Shakti Peetha
Karnataka Kashi and the Mahalakshmi Shakti Peetha
Dakshina Kashi and the Jogulamba Shakti Peetha
x: Alampur is called Dakshina Kashi and contains the Jogulamba Shakti Peetha.

s: Which of the following places in Andhra are cited as examples of the Eastern Chalukyan transmission of the Vesara or Chalukyan style?
x: Bikkavolu and Draksharama are cited as Andhra examples of the Vesara or Chalukyan style carried by the Eastern Chalukyas.

s: The Navabrahma temples at Alampur are built in which style?
x: The nine Navabrahma temples are Nagara with rekha shikharas, not Dravida.

s: In which present-day district are the Alampur Navabrahma temples located?
x: Alampur lies in Jogulamba Gadwal district of Telangana, on the Tungabhadra.

s: How many temples make up the Navabrahma group at Alampur?
x: The Navabrahma group has nine early Badami Chalukya Shiva temples.

s: Which dynasty built the Navabrahma temples at Alampur?
x: The nine Navabrahma Shiva temples at Alampur were built by the early Badami Chalukyas in the 7th-8th centuries.

s: Under which dynasty did temple building in Andhra begin?
x: Temple building in Andhra began under the Ikshvakus.

s: Alampur is known as the western gateway of which shrine?
x: Alampur, also called Dakshina Kashi, is the western gateway of Srisailam.

s: The Vesara style of temple architecture is mainly associated with which region?
o: North India, north of the Vindhyas
South India, between the Krishna and the Kaveri
The Deccan, between the Vindhyas and the Krishna
x: Vesara is the Deccan style of the region between the Vindhyas and the Krishna.

s: What is the defining feature of the Dravida temple style?
o: A flat slab roof without a tower
x: Dravida temples are marked by a pyramidal vimana and gopurams; the curvilinear shikhara marks Nagara.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Vesara style:
1. It is a hybrid of the Nagara and Dravida styles.
2. It uses a Dravida plan with Nagara details.
3. It is mainly found north of the Vindhyas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Vesara is a Nagara-Dravida hybrid with a Dravida plan and Nagara details; it belongs to the Deccan, not north of the Vindhyas.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the phases of Badami Chalukyan temple architecture?
o: Aihole represents the experimental structural phase
Pattadakal represents the earliest, rock-cut phase
x: Pattadakal is the mature, final phase; the sequence runs from the rock-cut caves of Badami to the experimental temples of Aihole and then Pattadakal.

s: According to Percy Brown's assessment, the Chalukyas were significant because they:
o: Introduced the first gopurams into Tamil Nadu
Were the first to break the monopoly of the rock-cut tradition in the Deccan
Abandoned structural temples in favour of Buddhist caves
Developed the Nagara style exclusively in North India
x: Percy Brown credited the Chalukyas with being the first to break the monopoly of the rock-cut tradition in the Deccan.

s: Which of the four main Badami cave temples is a Jain cave?
x: Badami has four principal sandstone caves of the 6th-7th centuries, the earliest made under Mangalesha; the fourth cave is Jain.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Cave 4 — Shiva — earliest cave of the complex
x: Cave 4 is a Jain cave, not a Shiva cave. Cave 1 is associated with Shiva, while the earliest caves were made during Mangalesha's period.

s: How many main cave temples are there at Badami?
x: Badami has four main sandstone caves around Agastya lake; Caves 1-3 are Hindu and Cave 4 is Jain.

s: Which Badami cave is the largest and bears Mangalesha's inscription of 578 CE?
x: Cave 3, dedicated to Vishnu, is the largest and carries Mangalesha's inscription of 578 CE.

s: The 18-armed Nataraja is found in which Badami cave?
x: Cave 1 is dedicated to Shiva and has the 18-armed Nataraja; Cave 4 is Jain.

s: Around which lake are the Badami cave temples located?
x: The four main Badami cave temples are cut in the sandstone hills around Agastya lake.

s: The architectural importance of Pattadakal lies especially in the fact that it:
o: Represents the exclusive triumph of the Nagara style in the Deccan
Contains only rock-cut temples of the Badami period
Was built entirely without royal patronage
Contains Nagara and Dravida temples standing side by side
x: Pattadakal displays Nagara and Dravida temple forms side by side and represents the mature phase of Chalukyan architecture.

s: How did K. A. Nilakanta Sastri describe Aihole?
x: K. A. Nilakanta Sastri described Aihole as the “Cradle of Indian temple architecture.”

s: Which temple at Aihole has the earliest massive bracket capital?
x: The Lad Khan temple, rectangular with a flat roof and stone grilles (and no shikhara), has the earliest massive bracket capital.

s: What is the plan of the Durga temple at Aihole?
o: Apsidal or gajaprishtha, with a pillared gallery around the shrine
Square, with a pyramidal vimana and four gopurams
Rectangular, with a flat roof and stone grilles
x: The Durga temple has an apsidal, or gajaprishtha, plan and a pillared gallery running around the shrine.

s: The Lad Khan temple at Aihole has which kind of roof?
o: A flat slab roof with no shikhara
A rekha shikhara on an apsidal plan
x: Lad Khan is rectangular with a flat slab roof and no shikhara.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Lad Khan — Aihole — flat stone-slab roof
Durga Temple — Aihole — apsidal plan with Nagara shikhara
Ravana Phadi — Aihole — rock-cut cave with a tower
x: Ravana Phadi is a rock-cut cave at Aihole without a tower. The other three pairs are correctly matched.

s: Which of the following pairs of temples both have a Nagara shikhara?
x: Huchimalligudi at Aihole and the Dashavatara temple at Deogarh have Nagara shikharas (UPSC 2026 key). Malegitti Shivalaya and Virupaksha are Dravida, and so are Meguti and Sangameshvara, so every other pair includes at least one Dravida temple.

s: Which Jain temple at Aihole is built in the Dravida style and bears the Aihole inscription?
x: The Meguti Jain temple at Aihole is Dravida and bears the Aihole inscription.

s: Which of the following temple – style pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: The Kashi Vishwanatha temple at Pattadakal is Nagara, not Dravida; the other pairs are correct.

s: Which temple at Pattadakal is built in the Nagara style?
x: The Papanatha temple is in the Nagara style; the Virupaksha, Mallikarjuna and Sangameshvara temples are Dravida.

s: The narrative friezes at Pattadakal depict scenes from the Ramayana, the Mahabharata and which other work?
x: Pattadakal is noted for narrative friezes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Panchatantra, along with Nandi mandapas and polished pillars.

s: The Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal copies the tradition of which temple?
x: The Dravida-style Virupaksha temple copies the Pallava Kailasanatha tradition of Kanchi, a line continued by the Rashtrakuta Kailasa at Ellora.

s: In which year was Pattadakal inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
x: Pattadakal became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987.

s: Which Badami Chalukya site was the royal coronation site?
x: Pattadakal served as the royal coronation site of the Badami Chalukyas.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Pattadakal – UNESCO site with Nagara and Dravida temples side by side
x: Pattadakal is a UNESCO site with Nagara and Dravida temples side by side. Badami is known for rock-cut caves, Aihole for early experimental temples, and Vesara is the hybrid style.

s: The Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal was built to mark Vikramaditya II's victory over which dynasty?
x: Queen Lokamahadevi built the Virupaksha temple for Vikramaditya II's victory over the Pallavas.

s: Who was Ravikirti, associated with the Meguti inscription at Aihole?
x: Ravikirti was the poet and composer named in the Aihole Meguti inscription, not the architect of the temple.

s: The inscriptions at the Virupaksha temple, Pattadakal, name which individuals as architects or sutradharis?
x: The Virupaksha temple inscriptions name the architects Gunda Anivaritachari and Sarvasiddhi Acharya.

s: To the patronage of which Pallava ruler is the Kudumiamalai music inscription credited?
x: The Kudumiamalai music inscription is credited to the patronage of Mahendravarman I, a king skilled in music, painting and literature.

s: Who converted the Pallava king Mahendravarman I from Jainism to Shaivism?
x: Mahendravarman I began as a Jain and was converted to Shaivism by Appar (Tirunavukkarasar), not Sambandar.

s: The inscriptional claim that a temple was built without brick, timber, metal or mortar is associated with which site?
x: The Mandagapattu cave temple carries the celebrated claim that it was constructed without brick, timber, metal or mortar.

s: Which of the following titles did NOT belong to Mahendravarman I?
x: Vatapikonda (conqueror of Vatapi) was the title of Narasimhavarman I; the others were Mahendravarman I's.

s: Who is the author of the Sanskrit farce Mattavilasa Prahasana?
x: The Pallava king Mahendravarman I wrote the Mattavilasa Prahasana; one of his titles was Mattavilasa.

s: Whom does the Mattavilasa Prahasana of Mahendravarman I make fun of?
x: The Mattavilasa Prahasana is a Sanskrit farce that mocks Kapalikas and Buddhist monks and shows the social and religious life of the time.

s: Which Pallava ruler began the rock-cut temples of South India?
x: Mahendravarman I was a great builder of cave temples; rock-cut temples in South India start with him.

s:
Consider the following statements about Mahendravarman I:
1. Rock-cut temples in South India begin with him.
2. He was a Shaiva who later became a Jain under the influence of Appar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Rock-cut temples in South India begin with Mahendravarman I. He began as a Jain and was turned to Shaivism by Appar, so statement 2 is wrong.

s: The Kudumiamalai inscription of the Pallava period is famous for which subject?
x: The Kudumiamalai inscription is a music inscription; it shows the royal interest in music.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the theories proposed regarding the origin of the Pallavas?
o: Scythian origin from the north-western frontier
x: The major theories mentioned are Parthian or Pahlava origin, Andhra origin and local Tamil origin in Tondaimandalam. A Scythian-origin theory is not included.

s: The Andhra-origin theory of the Pallavas is supported chiefly by which combination of evidence?
o: Their association with the Kaveri delta and Chola inscriptions
Their Sanskrit inscriptions and control of Vatapi
Early Prakrit charters from the Krishna-Guntur region and replacement of the Ikshvakus
x: The Andhra-origin theory draws support from early Prakrit charters found in the Krishna-Guntur region and the Pallavas’ replacement of the Ikshvakus there.

s: Which was the capital of the Pallavas?
x: The Pallavas ruled Tondaimandalam from Kanchipuram; Vatapi was the Chalukya capital.

s: What was the traditional territory of the Pallavas called?
x: Tondaimandalam was the traditional territory associated with the Pallavas, with Kanchipuram as their capital.

s: Who issued the Prakrit Mayidavolu plates, among the earliest Pallava records, as yuvaraja?
x: The Mayidavolu plates were issued by Sivaskandavarman as yuvaraja; the Manchikallu inscription belongs to the Pallava Simhavarman.

s:
Consider the following statements about the end of the Ikshvakus:
1. Rudrapurushadatta was the last Ikshvaku ruler, defeated by the Pallavas.
2. He was defeated by Simhavishnu, founder of the imperial Pallava line.
3. The victory helped establish Pallava rule in the Krishna valley.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Pallava Simhavarman (not Simhavishnu) defeated the last Ikshvaku ruler Rudrapurushadatta, helping establish Pallava rule in the Krishna valley.

s: To which ruler do the Hirahadagalli plates, recording the Agnishtoma, Vajapeya and Ashvamedha sacrifices, belong?
x: The Prakrit Hirahadagalli plates are of Sivaskandavarman, who performed these sacrifices.

s: The Renati Chodas were early feudatories of which dynasty?
x: The Renati Chodas were early Pallava feudatories.

s: Which inscription records the Pallava conquest of Vijayapuri after the defeat of the Ikshvakus?
x: The Manchikallu inscription of Simhavarman proves that the Pallavas replaced the Ikshvakus of Vijayapuri.

s: Which Pallava ruler issued the Manchikallu inscription?
x: The Manchikallu inscription belongs to Simhavarman, who defeated the last Ikshvaku ruler Rudrapurushadatta.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Mayidavolu plates were issued by Sivaskandavarman as yuvaraja.
2. The Manchikallu inscription belongs to the Ikshvakus of Vijayapuri.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are Pallava records: Mayidavolu of Sivaskandavarman and Manchikallu of Simhavarman, who conquered the Ikshvaku land, so statement 2 is wrong.

s: Which of the following Pallava ruler – event pairs is correctly matched?
x: Vishnugopa faced Samudragupta's invasion. Sivaskandavarman is linked with Kanchi coming under Pallava control, Simhavishnu defeated the Kalabhras and Narasimhavarman I took Vatapi.

s: Who killed Aparajita, bringing the Pallava dynasty to an end?
x: Aditya I Chola killed Aparajita, bringing the Pallava dynasty to an end around 897–898 CE.

s: Which Pallava ruler, founder of the imperial line, defeated the Kalabhras?
x: Simhavishnu (c. 575-600) founded the imperial line and defeated the Kalabhras.

s:
Arrange the following Pallava rulers in chronological order:
1. Simhavishnu
2. Nandivarman II
3. Narasimhavarman I
4. Paramesvaravarman I
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: The main line runs Simhavishnu, Mahendravarman I, Narasimhavarman I, Paramesvaravarman I, Narasimhavarman II and then Nandivarman II.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Pallava ruler)
A. Simhavishnu
B. Mahendravarman I
C. Nandivarman II
D. Aparajita
List-II (Event)
1. Lost Kanchi for a time to Vikramaditya II
2. Defeated the Kalabhras
3. Killed by Aditya I Chola
4. Lost Krishna-Godavari lands to Pulakesin II
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Simhavishnu defeated the Kalabhras, Mahendravarman I lost land to Pulakesin II, Nandivarman II lost Kanchi to Vikramaditya II, and Aparajita was killed by Aditya I Chola.

s: Under which Pallava ruler did Kanchi come under the Pallavas?
x: Kanchi came under the Pallavas in the time of the early ruler Sivaskandavarman; Vishnugopa faced Samudragupta's invasion.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Kanchi came under the Pallavas during the reign of Sivaskandavarman.
2. Simhavishnu faced the invasion of Samudragupta.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Kanchi came under the Pallavas under Sivaskandavarman; it was Vishnugopa, not Simhavishnu, who faced Samudragupta.

s: Nandivarman II Pallavamalla came to the throne under which circumstances?
o: He was appointed by Vikramaditya II after the fall of Kanchi.
He inherited the throne directly from Simhavishnu as his eldest son.
He was elected by the public as an adult military commander.
He was chosen as a twelve-year-old by ministers and nobles from a collateral line.
x: After the death of Paramesvaravarman II around 731 CE, ministers and nobles selected Nandivarman II, a twelve-year-old from a collateral line.

s: Which Pallava ruler built the Vaikuntha Perumal temple at Kanchi?
x: Nandivarman II Pallavamalla, an ardent Vaishnavite and contemporary of Tirumangai Alvar, built the Vaikuntha Perumal temple at Kanchi.

s: Who among the following was a contemporary of Nandivarman II, an ardent Vaishnavite?
x: Nandivarman II was a contemporary of Tirumangai Alvar; Appar is linked to Mahendravarman I.

s: Which Pallava ruler bore the title Pallavamalla?
x: Nandivarman II, chosen king from a collateral line, bore the title Pallavamalla.

s: Around which year did the Pallava dynasty end with the killing of Aparajita?
x: Aditya I Chola killed Aparajita c. 897 CE, ending the Pallava dynasty.

s: Which of the following was NOT one of the later Pallava rulers?
x: Simhavishnu was the founder of the imperial line (c. 575-600); Dantivarman, Nandivarman III and Nripatunga were later Pallavas.

s: Where was Mayurasharman insulted by a Pallava horseman before he founded the Kadamba kingdom?
x: According to the Talagunda inscription, Mayurasharman, a Brahmin student at the Kanchi Ghatika, was insulted by a Pallava horseman and subsequently took up arms and founded the Kadamba kingdom.

s: In whose court did Bharavi, author of the Kiratarjuniya, live?
x: Bharavi was at Simhavishnu's court.

s: Who is the author of the Dashakumaracharita and the Kavyadarsha?
x: Dandin of the Pallava court wrote the Dashakumaracharita and Kavyadarsha.

s: Which writer of the Pallava court called Vengi 'Andhra Nagaram'?
x: Dandin called Vengi 'Andhra Nagaram'.

s:
Consider the following statements about Mayurasharman:
1. He was a Brahmin student at the Kanchi Ghatika.
2. After being insulted by a Pallava horseman, he founded the Chalukya kingdom.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Mayurasharman studied at the Kanchi Ghatika; after the insult he founded the Kadamba kingdom, not the Chalukya kingdom.

s: During whose reign did Hiuen Tsang visit Kanchi around 640 CE?
x: Hiuen Tsang visited Kanchi c. 640 CE, in the reign of Narasimhavarman I.

s: What was a Ghatika in the Pallava period?
o: A Brahminical college of Vedic learning
x: A Ghatika was a Brahminical (Vedic) college of Brahmin scholars, usually attached to temples; Kanchi had a famous one.

s: In which language was learning mainly carried on at the Pallava Ghatikas?
x: The Ghatikas were Brahminical colleges where the medium of learning was Sanskrit.

s: Which inscription records how Mayurasharman founded the Kadamba kingdom?
x: The Talagunda inscription tells how Mayurasharman, insulted at the Kanchi Ghatika, took up arms and founded the Kadamba kingdom.

s: Which dynasty pioneered Dravida temple art in South India?
x: The Pallavas pioneered Dravida temple art; under them the Grantha script spread and the Alvar-Nayanar Bhakti movement grew.

s: Which script of the Pallava period became the parent of several Southeast Asian scripts?
x: The Grantha script of the Pallavas is the parent of many Southeast Asian scripts.

s: The Grantha script, which became the parent of several Southeast Asian scripts, is associated with which dynasty?
x: The Grantha script developed under the Pallavas and spread to Southeast Asia.

s: Where did Narasimhavarman I defeat and kill Pulakesin II in 642 CE?
x: Narasimhavarman I killed Pulakesin II at Manimangala in 642 CE and sacked Vatapi through his general Paranjoti.

s:
Consider the following statements about Narasimhavarman I:
1. He bore the titles Mamalla ('great wrestler') and Vatapikonda.
2. Mahabalipuram is called Mamallapuram after him.
3. Vichitrachitta was one of his titles.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct: Mamalla and Vatapikonda were his titles. Statement 2 is correct: Mamallapuram is named after him. Statement 3 is wrong: Vichitrachitta was a title of his father Mahendravarman I. So B; A misses statement 2, C and D include statement 3.

s: Narasimhavarman I sent naval expeditions to Sri Lanka primarily to:
o: support Pulakesin II against the Cholas
conquer the island for permanent Pallava rule
establish a Buddhist monastery at Kanchi
x: Narasimhavarman I sent two naval expeditions to Sri Lanka to restore his ally, Prince Manavarma.

s: Which general of Narasimhavarman I sacked Vatapi in 642 CE?
x: General Paranjoti sacked Vatapi after Pulakesin II was killed at Manimangala.

s: Which of the following architectural achievements is associated with Narasimhavarman I?
o: Construction of the first Kadamba capital at Banavasi
Construction of the monolithic rathas at Mahabalipuram
Construction of the Vaikuntha Perumal temple at Kanchi
x: Narasimhavarman I is associated with the monolithic rathas at Mahabalipuram and was a staunch Shaivite.

s: Which Pallava ruler is associated with the Pancha Rathas, Varaha Mandapa and Mahishasuramardini Cave at Mahabalipuram?
x: The Pancha Rathas, Varaha Mandapa and Mahishasuramardini Cave are attributed to Narasimhavarman I, also known as Mamalla.

s: During whose reign was the Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram built?
o: Narasimhavarman II, also known as Rajasimha
x: The Shore Temple is attributed to Narasimhavarman II, or Rajasimha, and is a structural temple.

s: Each of the Pancha Rathas at Mahabalipuram was carved out of a single rock of which kind?
x: The Pancha Rathas are monolithic, each carved from a single granite rock, imitating earlier wooden and structural forms.

s: Which is the largest ratha at Mahabalipuram and a precursor of the Dravida vimana?
x: The Dharmaraja ratha is the largest and a precursor of the Dravida vimana; the Draupadi ratha is the smallest, a hut-shaped single cell.

s: What is Arjuna's Penance, also known as the Descent of the Ganga?
o: A Jain cave mural depicting a lotus pond
A structural temple with three sanctums
The largest open-air rock relief in India depicting Bhagiratha's penance
A monolithic shrine dedicated exclusively to Vishnu
x: Arjuna's Penance or the Descent of the Ganga is the largest open-air rock relief in India and is associated with Bhagiratha's penance.

s: Besides two Shiva shrines, the Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram has a shrine of which deity?
x: The Shore Temple is a structural temple with two Shiva shrines and one Vishnu shrine, the surviving temple of the Seven Pagodas tradition.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its principal sculptural theme at Mahabalipuram?
x: Varaha Mandapa depicts Varaha rescuing Bhudevi. Krishna lifting Govardhana belongs to Krishna Mandapa, while Durga slaying Mahishasura belongs to Mahishasuramardini Cave.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Pancha Rathas at Mahabalipuram?
o: Each was built of brick and timber
x: Each ratha is a monolith carved from one granite rock, only copying wooden forms.

s: The Shore Temple is the only survivor of which group of temples?
x: The Shore Temple survives from the 'Seven Pagodas'; the other six are believed lost to the sea.

s: Who among the following Pallava rulers bore the title Mahamalla?
x: Narasimhavarman I was called Mamalla or Mahamalla ('great wrestler'), and Mamallapuram is named after him.

s: What is the theme of the main relief in the Krishna Mandapa at Mahabalipuram?
x: The Krishna Mandapa at Mahabalipuram shows Krishna lifting the Govardhana hill.

s: In which year was the Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List?
x: The Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram received UNESCO World Heritage status in 1984.

s: In which year was Ajanta inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List?
x: Ajanta was inscribed in 1983, a year before Mahabalipuram (1984); 1819 is when it was found.

s: Which of the following heritage sites was created by the Pallavas?
x: Mahabalipuram, with its open-air reliefs, rathas and structural temple, is the Pallava site; Ajanta is a cliff complex of cave paintings and monasteries, not Pallava.

s: Of how many viharas and chaityas does the Ajanta cave complex consist?
x: Ajanta has 25 viharas and 4 chaityas with Jataka paintings.

s: Who discovered the Ajanta caves in 1819?
x: The Ajanta caves were found in 1819 by John Smith, a British officer.

s: Mahabalipuram was a seventh-century port city of which dynasty?
x: Mahabalipuram was a 7th-century Pallava port city.

s: Who completed the construction of the Kailasanatha temple at Kanchi?
x: The Kailasanatha temple, rich in Shiva sculptures and a model for later Chola temples, was completed by Mahendravarman III.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Vaikuntha Perumal — Vishnu temple with a storeyed sanctum and panels on Pallava history
Kailasanatha — Buddhist monastery with Jataka paintings
Vaikuntha Perumal — Jain cave with a lotus-pond mural
Kailasanatha — three-shrine temple with two Vishnu shrines
x: Vaikuntha Perumal is a Vishnu temple with a storeyed sanctum and panels depicting Pallava history.

s: The Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal was modelled on which Pallava monument?
x: The Pattadakal Virupaksha temple was modelled on the Pallava Kailasanatha temple at Kanchi.

s: Of which material is the Kailasanatha temple at Kanchi built?
x: The Kailasanatha is a sandstone temple; the Mahabalipuram rathas are granite.
